title: Conditional κ ≥ 0.00374039009039 (+0.27743% over #7704) by recoding the role-1256 relay cuts
body:
## Result

This construction gives **conditional κ ≥ 0.00374039009039** on the signed 16-stage P104 caller. It exceeds the upper endpoint of Clear1nsight’s #7704 graph by **0.00001034832006 (0.27743%)**. That increment is 2.48 times the 0.0000041662072 gain in #7674. The selected maintainer-reviewed reference at the base of this PR is 0.00363005817. [Parent and its tight bracket](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111#discussioncomment-19708867) · [Application receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f0e2db5b5b46b139da17d2b32fab6633164443a9/research/p104-relay-cut-recoding/results/application.json)

| Full application | #7704 | New construction |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Paid recursive jobs | 101,840 | 101,488 |
| Productive jobs | 21,152 | 21,152 |
| Paid rank mass | 271,568 | 271,568 |
| Local scalar terms per native call | 172,414 | 177,531 |
| Numeric bank homes per native call | 9,150 | 9,128 |
| Charged scalar services across the caller | 122,001,408 | 124,542,464 |
| Directed raw κ crossing | (0.00373004177032, 0.00373004177033) | (0.00374039009047, 0.00374039009048) |

## Construction and review

The input is the exact #7704 role-1256 graph, reconstructed from SYLforge’s #7700 source word. The ordered certificate has 22 eliminations, 21 grouped hub reroutes and three that recover a signal jointly from banks at two charts. At cut 38 the required signal has recovery denominator five. At cut 40, a sender routes a sum to chart 778, which previously received no edge from the old middle chart. Two paid rank-two jobs become ranks three and one. Cut 42 then reduces them to one rank-four job. This illustrates how one cut makes another possible. [Proof and worked examples](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f0e2db5b5b46b139da17d2b32fab6633164443a9/research/p104-relay-cut-recoding/PROOF.md) · [Exact witnesses](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f0e2db5b5b46b139da17d2b32fab6633164443a9/research/p104-relay-cut-recoding/CUTS.json)

- Every intermediate graph has an acyclic schedule and strictly nested replacement routes. Each saved identity is checked on independent inputs. Forward replay checks all 1,501 public rows with 9,280,471 exact products. A separate reverse accumulation compares all 1,501 parent and candidate columns.
- The native checker verifies rank, signed Pauli action and absolute phase on 3,023 chart pairs. For all 54 distinct changed pairs on surviving slots it also checks 512 forward and 512 adjoint columns. All 104 main adapters and 1,664 port-stage contact bindings are replayed.
- The complete paid histogram changes at ranks 1–7 by $(−288,+48,−368,+96,+80,+48,+32)$. The target histogram is identical. The exact concave-order comparison gives a strict decrease for every $r^t$, $0<t<1$. Two directed interval evaluators bracket the crossing. The compiler tests 0.00374039009046, and all 54 strict and four functional outer predicates pass.
- Physical replay includes 4,863,931 nonintegral-coefficient basis divisions at exact ticks, complete charged retirement, four guarded streams per stage and the higher scalar cost. The no-cancellation common-root guard passes with $c=1156$ at the candidate’s own $H=14617400000000000000$. [Physical and compiler receipts](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f0e2db5b5b46b139da17d2b32fab6633164443a9/research/p104-relay-cut-recoding/results/application.json)

The eight registered checks passed locally on arm64 macOS with Python 3.12.16 and the standard library. The standalone constructor emits the candidate graph with canonical SHA-256 `db10e4ca7154b454f86bf404bc34b3a16d02de6cc008d5227e4eef2654cb0778`. [Replay manifest](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f0e2db5b5b46b139da17d2b32fab6633164443a9/research/p104-relay-cut-recoding/VERIFY.json)

Main’s onboarding test failed locally because its CI guide specifies #6030 while the selected record specifies #7000. The prerequisite matches all five original file blobs, and all six navigation/status tests pass with it applied. ## Verification at the published head

GitHub passed planning, the historical prerequisite replay and all eight registered scientific checks on `7017edbe4bc5ed1b6d5b6defedbc7e472d83c65c`. A Git-free export of the 48 package files and four declared inputs passed all eight checks and reproduced the candidate SHA-256. A fresh full-history clone also verified the committed bytes, file modes and source-commit ancestry. All 27 files in the external source inventory matched the Git blob at their stated original commit. At the parent’s upper endpoint 0.00373004177033, direct 256-bit interval evaluation places the new target-minus-paid margin between 3.64608447709 and 3.64608447710. [Hosted scientific replay](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/44322431218/job/134867733284) · [Complete run](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/44322431218)

A separate local dense replay executed all 6,121 paid routes on the full 512-coordinate arrays. For each of the four input fixtures in the parent’s published DENSE.json, the SHA-256 of the 1,501 physical output arrays matched its pre-existing oracle. The fixtures cover two primes. They supply an end-to-end phase and scalar check at width 512. [Upstream public oracles](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e29a5ae8591243c1178067727f12ce4abefa0b93/research/cf6a-banked-role1256-relay/evidence/DENSE.json)

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the supplemental finite-field check</summary>

Use the candidate checkout as the first argument, the scientific package directory of #7704 at `e29a5ae8591243c1178067727f12ce4abefa0b93` as the second, and the canonical JSON emitted by `recoding.py` as the third. The script runs with isolated Python 3.12 and the standard library.

```python
"""Check the exported candidate against the dense public oracles published in PR 7704."""
from functools import cache
from pathlib import Path
from random import Random
from sys import argv, path
import json

root, old = (Path(s).resolve() for s in argv[1:3])
path.insert(0, str(old / "dense_support"))
path.insert(0, str(root / "research/shared-wire-split-composition/frozen"))
import clifford_exact as cliff
import native_verify
from field_interpreter import GateInterpreter, digest

def require(test, message):
    if not test:
        raise ValueError(message)

g = json.loads(Path(argv[3]).read_bytes())
receipts = json.loads((old / "evidence/DENSE.json").read_bytes())["fields"]
moves = {k: (a, b) for k, a, b in g["moves"]}
forms = dict(g["forms"])

@cache
def chart(i):
    return cliff.canonical_frame(9, tuple(g["frames"][i]))

@cache
def body(a, b):
    recipe, _ = cliff.lower_child(chart(a).adjoint().then(chart(b)))
    return native_verify.recipe(recipe)

for field in receipts:
    p = field["prime"]
    engine = GateInterpreter(p, require)
    coeff = cache(engine.coefficient)

    @cache
    def prepared(a, b):
        return tuple(engine.gate(gate) for gate in body(a, b))

    for case in field["cases"]:
        rng = Random(case["seed"])
        banks = {~r: [rng.randrange(p) for _ in range(512)] for r in range(len(g["initial"]))}
        require(digest(banks.values()) == case["inputs_sha256"], "input fixture")
        for key in g["schedule"]:
            row = [0] * 512
            for donor, literal in forms[key]:
                q = coeff(literal)
                row = [(x + q * y) % p for x,y in zip(row, banks[donor], strict=True)]
            banks[key] = engine.apply(prepared(*moves[key]), row) if key in moves else row
        actual = digest(banks[g["first_output"] + r] for r in range(len(g["final"])))
        require(actual == case["oracle_sha256"], "typed dense output")
        print("PASS_DENSE_CUT_GRAPH", p, case["seed"], actual, flush=True)
```

</details>
